{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABZjiq8w", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhDKRN4", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 87, "title": "Implement Ap µPD4990A Time Set/Counter Hold", "body": "## Problem

Ap guests cannot set the RTC through its hardware interface. At baseline `b503300c78dc6f748c0ae637f95b947cb4540e41`, [Rtc::write](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/b503300c78dc6f748c0ae637f95b947cb4540e41/src/rtc.rs#L155) accepts only commands 0, 1 and 3. Command 2 leaves the previous mode active, while `tick` always advances the calendar. Guest Time Set sequences therefore neither load nor hold the counter.

Implement this one missing register-control command, completing a prerequisite for future BIOS calendar-setting services.

## Expected outcome

Implement parallel `010` and serial `0010` through the existing Ap ports.

Required hardware semantics: STB rising transfers the 40-bit parallel calendar, with year ineffective, or the 48-bit serial calendar including year. Data is LSB-first: seconds, minutes, hours, day, month-high/weekday-low, then serial year; fields are BCD except hexadecimal month. Time Set holds the counter and calendar shift register, outputs the register LSB, and permits independent serial command-register shifting. Commands 0/1/3 release the counter. Entry and release reset divider stages 10–15 while lower stages continue running. Follow [NEC µPD4990A IC-1755, printed pp.4, 6–7 and Figures 1–5](https://www.renesas.com/en/document/dst/upd4990a-data-sheet).

Use deterministic guest clocks. Preserve the stored year during parallel setting, prevent accumulated held time from becoming catch-up seconds, and expose the set calendar through existing serial reads and BIOS snapshots.

Scope: valid calendar loading, hold, DATA OUT, divider phase, release and existing reset retention. BIOS setting services, TP/interval/IRQ/test commands, VM RTC behavior, host synchronization and electrical tolerances remain separate. Document invalid-data handling without claiming unspecified silicon behavior.

## Context and reproduction

Relevant existing paths:

- [RTC implementation](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/b503300c78dc6f748c0ae637f95b947cb4540e41/src/rtc.rs): calendar, shift registers and clock fraction.
- [RTC tests](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/b503300c78dc6f748c0ae637f95b947cb4540e41/tests/rtc.rs): port framing, rollover, batching, reset and BIOS INT/IRET checks.
- [Original guest](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/b503300c78dc6f748c0ae637f95b947cb4540e41/guest/rtc.asm), [provenance manifest](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/b503300c78dc6f748c0ae637f95b947cb4540e41/fixtures/rtc-manifest.json) and [browser regression](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/b503300c78dc6f748c0ae637f95b947cb4540e41/tests/browser/rtc.spec.js).

Reproduction: enter Shift, clock a valid calendar into the register, strobe Time Set, then inspect BIOS AH=00 and advance guest clocks. Current code ignores Time Set; expected behavior follows the contract above. Serial loading must account for the complete 52-bit data/command chain rather than accidentally shifting the calendar while framing the final command.

Project progress: PR #86 completed bounded single-head multi-sector non-DMA FDC writes. The Coordinator reports 341 native passes, 115 focused passes and 122 production-Wasm browser passes; [the validation record](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/b503300c78dc6f748c0ae637f95b947cb4540e41/docs/validation.md#issue-85-single-head-multi-sector-fdc-non-dma-write-data) records initial failures and corrections. No independent review or remote CI report was supplied. These results were not rerun by this evaluator.

All 26 inventory categories retain their required scopes and statuses: 23 partial, GRCG implemented_unverified, paging/FPU unimplemented, none verified. Protected mode, paging and basic x87 remain required. No supplied open Issue duplicates this task.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add an original port-driven reproduction that fails against the baseline, then implement the complete command contract above through ports `20h`/`33h`; use literal expected results independent of production decoding.
- [ ] Cover both command forms, every calendar field, parallel year preservation, serial command-tail framing, both LSB values, unchanged control writes, held CLK activity, and release through each of commands 0/1/3. Check unrelated system-port bits remain unchanged.
- [ ] Exercise the specified divider behavior with multiple initial phases and hold durations, including boundary-adjacent clocks. For the repository’s 8 MHz scheduler, the derived 64 Hz period is 125,000 clocks. Use an independent divider reference; a full-phase reset shortcut must fail. Compare small, irregular and maximum-sized tick batches, including repeated Time Set and reset while held.
- [ ] Verify guest-written dates using literal serial and BIOS-byte oracles, including a month transition, a serial leap-day transition and two-digit year rollover. Confirm BIOS INT/IRET register/flag contracts and destination guards remain intact. Malformed payloads must not cause host panics or memory corruption.
- [ ] Add an original MIT source-built `rtc_set` guest probe with an offline builder and checked provenance manifest recording source/license, assembly command, hashes, result layout and execution budget. Guest instructions must perform setting, elapsed-time hold checks, release and BIOS comparison. Expected results must be independently specified.
- [ ] Boot the identical probe natively and in production release-Wasm at both `/` and `/pc98-rust/`, cold and after reset. Assert exact result bytes, guards, unchanged media, PASS, absence of errors and at most 8,000,000 slots per boot. Await completed browser media mounting. Hosts may mount, step, inspect and reset; they must not inject RTC state or patch results.
- [ ] Preserve existing RTC read/reset probes and all DOS/apps/VM/audio, FDC/DMA/PIC, IDE and six-game assertions and budgets. After documented legal fixture preparation, the Coordinator runs `cargo test --locked --test rtc --test timer`, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `git diff --check` and `npm test`. Integrate the new probe into README preparation and CI. Report exact outcomes and any failures; acquire no commercial ROMs or guest software.
- [ ] Update RTC documentation and validation evidence, qualifying existing phase wording for Time Set release. RTC remains partial: BIOS setting, TP/interval/IRQ/test controls, VM behavior and broader acceptance remain outstanding. Limited probes and game regressions establish neither full accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
